The remaining gap from the current parent bound to the target is very small, and the parent was already produced by a dense family of active-LP, pair-move, and binary-search heuristics. The proposed method changes the primary update mechanism: instead of staying in a local active-constraint linearization and taking *linear-direction* line searches from one parent seed, search a smoothed correlation envelope with **proximal water-filling moves, Frank–Wolge/von Neumann oracle endpoints, soft-gradient directions, and mass-exchange coordinate moves**, keep all information combined and run it through **a strict population driver on the exact evaluator**.

The central mathematical misconception avoided is treating the evaluator as a circular or periodic overlap. The implementation must use only the finite-support correlation metric

    C5(h) = max_r dx * np.correlate(h, 1 - h, mode="full")[r],

with `dx = 2 / n_points`, and enforce both constraints through a **single joint feasible-set projection**.
